name: Milestones
tagline: A defined point within an ongoing measure that the system separately recognizes when the user reaches or crosses it, distinct from the running progress display itself.
desc: A milestone is a defined position along a broader measure the product already tracks, a balance, a duration, a count, a journey, rather than a standalone criterion of its own. What separates it from the ordinary progress display underneath it is a recognition event: the product distinguishes being short of the point from having reached it, and that crossing produces something observable beyond the number simply changing, a marker, a message, a state change. The measure can keep moving past the point once it's crossed, and the same threshold definition can recur across separate seasons, accounts, or journeys without losing its status as a milestone each time.
principle: A milestone is a position, not a total. The measure underneath it can be read on its own, but the milestone only exists at the moment the product treats one specific point along that measure as worth recognizing on its own terms.
warn: The label is easy to claim from an ordinary level-up or balance update that the product never actually singles out: if crossing the point produces nothing beyond the running number changing, no separate marker, message, or state, it's progression on display rather than a recognized milestone. The reverse risk sits in language rather than behavior: copy that calls a moment a milestone doesn't make it one without a defined point in a broader measure behind it.
variants: Threshold milestone, reached when a measurable value meets or crosses a defined amount
Time-based milestone, reached when a defined duration, anniversary, or tenure elapses within an ongoing relationship or activity
Cumulative milestone, the threshold depends on activity, value, or time accumulated across multiple occurrences
Unlocking milestone, reaching it changes access to a feature, area, tier, or capability
Recurring milestone, the same threshold can be reached again within repeated periods, seasons, or accounts
lifecycle: Needs an ongoing measure already established before any point along it can be recognized, so it has nothing to mark immediately after signup. Most visible once a user is close enough to the next defined point to see it as reachable.
